note: realms.json - the worlds a login may send a player to, as an operator writes them. The same rows live in the login database's realmlist table (the reference's own home for them, docs/decisions/0005-json-configuration.md); a row here with an id the table holds overrides it field by field, and a row with a new id is added. A field this file does not state keeps the table's value, and a world only this file states starts from the reference's defaults.

information.what: A world's address and port are the operator's choice, so they belong in a settings file as well as in the table.
information.how it is read: Once at start-up, after the table. The program logs how many rows came from this file.
information.what is not here: Anything a player does (accounts and characters are rows in the database), and anything the client dictates.

realms.name: Kryta
realms.doc: The world this machine serves. The id is the map token a client carries back on its gameplay connection, so it must match a realmlist row's id; the port is where the world program will listen and is what a login hands out.
